messages.content: What parameters do the viscous friction force depend on, and in which case should it be taken into account for the physical pendulum model? In your response the last word of each sentence must become the first word of the next sentence.

message.content: The viscous friction force in a rotational system depends on the angular velocity and the viscous damping coefficient. Coefficient b is determined by the dynamic viscosity of the surrounding fluid, the surface area of the body, and its geometric shape. Shape and area become relevant whenever the pendulum swings through air, water, or any other resistive medium. Medium-induced damping should be incorporated into the physical pendulum model when the energy loss per cycle is non-negligible compared to the total mechanical energy. Energy dissipation makes the ideal undamped model inaccurate in cases involving low angular velocities, high fluid viscosity, or precision timing applications. Applications such as laboratory torsion pendulums or chronometric devices require this correction for accurate period predictions.
